entities.summary: Buonaccorso Pitti (1350-1430) was a prominent Florentine merchant and member of the powerful Pitti family, whose patriarch, Cosimo de' Medici, played a crucial role in shaping the city's politics. Born into a family of great influence, Pitti's own life was marked by both financial success and personal risk, as he engaged in numerous high-stakes business deals and gamble with his fortune. His diary, a rare and valuable historical artifact, has provided scholars with a unique glimpse into the inner workings of 15th-century Florence. Pitti's legacy is also tied to the city's cultural and artistic developments, as he was a patron of the arts and a collector of rare books. Through his connections to the powerful Medici family, Pitti's influence extended beyond Florence, shaping the course of Italian history. His story serves as a testament to the complex web of relationships and alliances that defined the Renaissance era. The Pitti family's involvement in the Pazzi conspiracy, a failed plot to overthrow the Medici, further highlights Pitti's involvement in the intrigue-ridden world of Renaissance politics. The enduring impact of Pitti's life and legacy can be seen in the continued prominence of the Pitti family in modern-day Florence, where their historic palaces and art collections remain a source of civic pride. In the words of Pitti himself, ' Fortune favours the brave,' a phrase that encapsulates his own life story and the enduring spirit of the Pitti family.
